full_judgment:
In Civil Revision No. 383 of 1985 a simple question falls for determination is whether written statement can be filed after the suit, on appeal from a preliminary decree, remitted to the trial Court for a limited purpose for alloting saham to the defendants who were not given saham by the trial Court. 

 3. The opposite party hereinbefore filed a partition suit praying for saham in respect of the land on various pretexts. The written statement filed by the petitioner-defendant No. 88 on 18.8.84 was rejected by the trial Court on 27.8.84. The trial Court decreed the suit in preliminary form. Against the preliminary decree made on 30.8.84 the defendants Nos. 30, 31, 36, and 61 preferred appeal which was allowed by the lower appellate Court and the decree of the trial Court was set aside and the lower Appellate Court remitted the suit to the trial Court for allocating saham to the defendants-appellants, After remand the defendant No. 88 the petitioner before me filed an application under section 151 CPC for accepting the written statement which was earlier rejected by the trial Court and the trial Court rejected the application by the impugned order. 

 6. In Civil Revision Case No. 605 of 1985 a simple question involved is whether the learned District Judge committed an error of law in rejecting an application filed under section 151 read with section 152 of the CPC to modify the decree made on 13.3.1984. It is contended on behalf of the petitioners that for the ends of justice the lower appellate Court ought to have modified the decree without sending the same to the trial Court to allocate the Saham. The impugned order is made under section 151 CPC. The said provision of law has no application in a case where an order passed against a party has alternative remedy. The order of remand can be challenged before the superior Court under provision of the Code. Therefore I do not find any substance in this contention of the learned Advocate. The learned Advocate for the petitioner candidly concedes that section 152 CPC is not applicable to the facts of the present case. Provision of section 152 CPC is attracted where clerical or arithmetical mistakes in judgments, decrees or orders occur or errors from any accidental slip or omission arise therein. As the judgment made by the lower appellate Court on remand was made on consideration of the facts and there is no accidental slip or omission as contemplated under section 152 CPC no correction of the decree can be made by the trial Court upon an application filed under section 152 CPC.
